taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bacopa monnieri (L.) Wettst.; the later Pennell combination is an isonym widely used by U.S. sources.
look_here_first: Look for a low creeping wetland mat with fleshy, small, sessile oblong-to-obovate leaves and solitary pale blue-white flowers arising from the leaf axils.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Harvard University Herbaria specimen from Aquarena Springs, San Marcos. Travis — Harvard specimens from the Colorado River at Austin. Comal — Harvard specimen from New Braunfels. Kew recognizes Texas within the native range.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Three exact target-zone localities are used; no county inferred from ecoregion maps.

best_field_traits: small sessile fleshy oblong to obovate leaves
corolla white to bluish/pinkish and weakly 2-lipped
5 deeply divided calyx lobes with unequal outer/inner lobes
small ovoid capsule retained within persistent calyx
morphology_keys.habit: Low mat-forming aquatic to semiaquatic herb; stems creep and root at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Small fleshy sessile oblong, obovate or spatulate leaves with rounded tips.
morphology_keys.flower: Solitary axillary flowers, pale blue/white/pinkish, with a short fused corolla and four stamens.
morphology_keys.fruit: Small ovoid capsule within the persistent calyx.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's San Marcos River frames pair the creeping succulent habit with a close flower view, making the axillary flower plus fleshy-leaf combination easy to memorize.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the creeping node-rooting succulent habit, small sessile fleshy leaves, and solitary axillary pale flowers together; do not identify Bacopa from wet habitat alone.
